# Overview

{strainselect} helps choosing which bacterial strains to sequence from a
collection described by metadata (sampling context, matrix, region, sector,
year...). It offers two complementary methods:

- the **clustering method** (`assess_gower()`, `cstats_table()`,
  `select_silhouette()`) is suited when the number of strains that can be
  sequenced is limited. Strains are grouped into *k* clusters of similar
  strains and the best clustered strain of each cluster is selected, so that
  the selected strains are as different as possible from each other;
- the **profile method** (`prepare_upset()`, `define_profiles()`,
  `select_profiles()`) is suited when the number of strains to sequence is
  not limited. Strains sharing exactly the same metadata are grouped and one
  strain per group is selected, so that every distinct profile — including
  unique strains — is represented.

Both methods start with `prepare_input()`, which cleans the raw table.

The examples below use `salmonella_strains`, a table of 100 *Salmonella*
strains described by 22 variables, shipped with the package. The selection is
based on 6 variables: `CONTEXTE`, `MATRICE1`, `REGION`, `SECTEUR`, `LIEUPVT`
and the year extracted from `DATE_PRELEVEMENT`.

# Example data: salmonella_strains

`salmonella_strains` is available as soon as the package is loaded. The same
table is also shipped as a CSV file (`;` separator), which shows the expected
format of an input file:
`system.file("data_test.csv", package = "strainselect")`.

```{r function-salmonella_strains}
#' Example metadata of 100 *Salmonella* strains
#'
#' Metadata of 100 strains of *Salmonella enterica* serotype 1,4,\[5\],12:i:-
#' (monophasic variant of Typhimurium) collected in France in 2020, used in the
#' examples of the package. Column names and values are in French, as in the
#' original database.
#'
#' @format A data frame with 100 rows (one per strain) and 22 columns:
#'   \describe{
#'     \item{IDENTIFIANT}{strain identifier (unique);}
#'     \item{SEROTYPE}{serotype of the strain;}
#'     \item{COMMENTAIRE}{free-text description of the sample;}
#'     \item{SAMPLETYPE}{type of sample;}
#'     \item{CONTEXTE}{sampling context (surveillance, product alert,
#'       control programme...);}
#'     \item{PAYS}{country of sampling;}
#'     \item{MATRICE}{sampled matrix, most detailed level;}
#'     \item{MATRICE1}{sampled matrix, first level of grouping;}
#'     \item{MATRICE2}{sampled matrix, second level of grouping;}
#'     \item{NOM_DEPARTEMENT}{name of the French département of sampling;}
#'     \item{REGION}{French region of sampling;}
#'     \item{SECTEUR}{sector (human food, animal health and production,
#'       ecosystem...);}
#'     \item{NUMERO_DEPARTEMENT}{number of the French département;}
#'     \item{CODE_POSTAL}{postal code of the place of sampling;}
#'     \item{DATE_PRELEVEMENT}{date of sampling (`dd/mm/yyyy`);}
#'     \item{DATE_RECEPTION}{date of reception at the laboratory
#'       (`dd/mm/yyyy`);}
#'     \item{TYPE_ANALYSE}{type of analysis;}
#'     \item{ATYPIQUE}{flag for atypical strains;}
#'     \item{TYPE_DE_DONNEES}{type of data;}
#'     \item{BOX_NUMBER}{storage box of the strain;}
#'     \item{EMPLACEMENT}{position of the strain in the box;}
#'     \item{LIEUPVT}{place of sampling in the food chain (farm,
#'       slaughterhouse, industrial processing...).}
#'   }
#' @source Example data provided by the authors. The same table is available
#'   as a CSV file: `system.file("data_test.csv", package = "strainselect")`.
#' @family data preparation
#' @examples
"salmonella_strains"
```

# Preparing the data: prepare_input

Before using any of the methods, the dataset must be cleaned and contain only
the metadata on which the selection is based. `prepare_input()`:

- checks that strain identifiers are unique (and stops with the list of
  duplicated identifiers otherwise);
- uses the identifiers as row names;
- keeps only the selected metadata columns;
- optionally extracts the year (`ANNEE`) and/or the month (`MOIS`) from a date
  column;
- replaces missing values by `"unknown"` and converts every column to a factor.

Columns can be given by their names (recommended, as it is easier to read and
does not depend on the order of the columns) or by their positions. Dates are
read with `date_format`, `"%d/%m/%Y"` (e.g. `09/01/2020`) by default; use for
instance `date_format = "%Y-%m-%d"` for dates such as `2020-01-09`. A date
column already of class `Date` is used as is.

```{r function-prepare_input}
#' Prepare the metadata table used for strain selection
#'
#' Checks that strain identifiers are unique, keeps the metadata columns used
#' for the selection, optionally extracts the year and/or the month from a
#' date column, replaces missing values by `"unknown"` and converts every
#' column to a factor.
#'
#' @param data A data frame (or a matrix) with one row per strain.
#' @param col_select Names or positions of the metadata columns to keep. The
#'   identifier and date columns are always removed from this selection.
#'   Defaults to all columns.
#' @param id Name or position of the column containing the strain
#'   identifiers.
#' @param date Name or position of the date column, or `NULL` (default) if no
#'   date should be used. `0` is also accepted for "no date".
#' @param month If `TRUE`, a `MOIS` column with the month (`"01"` to `"12"`)
#'   is created from the date column.
#' @param year If `TRUE` (default), an `ANNEE` column with the year is created
#'   from the date column.
#' @param date_format Format of the dates, see [strptime()]. Defaults to
#'   `"%d/%m/%Y"` (e.g. `09/01/2020`). Ignored when the date column is
#'   already of class `Date` or `POSIXt`.
#' @param m,a Deprecated, use `month` and `year` instead.
#'
#' @return A data frame with one row per strain (row names are the strain
#'   identifiers) and one factor column per selected metadata, followed by
#'   `ANNEE` and/or `MOIS` when a date column is used. Dates that cannot be
#'   read give `"unknown"`.
#' @export
#' @family data preparation
#' @examples
prepare_input <- function (data, col_select = seq_len(ncol(data)), id = 1, date = NULL,
                           month = FALSE, year = TRUE, date_format = "%d/%m/%Y",
                           m, a) {
  if (!missing(m)) {
    warning("`m` is deprecated, use `month` instead.", call. = FALSE)
    month <- m
  }
  if (!missing(a)) {
    warning("`a` is deprecated, use `year` instead.", call. = FALSE)
    year <- a
  }
  data <- as.data.frame(data)
  id <- column_position(data, id, "id")
  col_select <- column_position(data, col_select, "col_select")
  if (isTRUE(all.equal(date, 0))) {
    date <- NULL
  }
  if (!is.null(date)) {
    date <- column_position(data, date, "date")
  }
  duplicate <- which(duplicated(data[,id]))
  if (length(duplicate)!=0) {
    stop ( "duplicate ID : " , paste(data[duplicate,id], collapse = ", "))
  } else {
    message("no duplicate ID")
  }
  rownames(data) <- data[,id]
  col_select <- col_select[! col_select %in% c(id, date)]
  clean_data <- data[, col_select, drop = FALSE]
  if (!is.null(date)){
    dates <- data[[date]]
    if (inherits(dates, c("Date", "POSIXt"))) {
      dates <- as.Date(dates)
    } else {
      dates <- as.Date(as.character(dates), format = date_format)
      if (all(is.na(dates)) && any(!is.na(data[[date]]))) {
        warning("no date could be read with date_format = \"", date_format,
                "\"; check the `date_format` argument.", call. = FALSE)
      }
    }
    if(year){
      clean_data$ANNEE <- format(dates, "%Y")
    }
    if(month){
      clean_data$MOIS <- format(dates, "%m")
    }
  }
  clean_data[is.na(clean_data)] <- "unknown"
  clean_data[] <- lapply(clean_data, factor)
  message("selected metadata: ", paste(colnames(clean_data), collapse = ", "))
  clean_data
}

#' Convert column names or positions into positions
#'
#' @param data A data frame.
#' @param x Column names (character) or positions (numeric).
#' @param arg Name of the argument, used in error messages.
#'
#' @return An integer vector of column positions.
#' @noRd
column_position <- function(data, x, arg) {
  if (is.character(x)) {
    pos <- match(x, names(data))
    if (anyNA(pos)) {
      stop("unknown column(s) in `", arg, "`: ",
           paste(x[is.na(pos)], collapse = ", "), call. = FALSE)
    }
    return(pos)
  }
  if (!is.numeric(x) || any(x < 1 | x > ncol(data))) {
    stop("`", arg, "` must be column names or positions between 1 and ",
         ncol(data), call. = FALSE)
  }
  as.integer(x)
}
```

```{r examples-prepare_input}
raw_data <- salmonella_strains
prepared_data <- prepare_input(
  raw_data,
  col_select = c("CONTEXTE", "MATRICE1", "REGION", "SECTEUR", "LIEUPVT"),
  id = "IDENTIFIANT", date = "DATE_PRELEVEMENT", month = FALSE, year = TRUE
)
head(prepared_data)
# the same with column positions
prepared_data <- prepare_input(raw_data, col_select = c(5, 8, 11, 12, 15, 22),
                               id = 1, date = 15)
```

```{r tests-prepare_input}
data_test <- matrix("test",nrow = 3,ncol = 5)
test_that("prepare_input works properly and show error if needed", {
  expect_error(prepare_input(data_test), "duplicate ID")
})

test_that("prepare_input selects columns, extracts dates and replaces NA", {
  raw <- data.frame(
    ID = c("s1", "s2", "s3"),
    HOST = c("pig", NA, "cattle"),
    DATE = c("09/01/2020", "15/03/2021", "30/12/2021"),
    COUNTRY = c("FR", "FR", "IT")
  )
  expect_message(
    res <- prepare_input(raw, col_select = 2:4, id = 1, date = 3, month = TRUE, year = TRUE),
    "no duplicate ID"
  )
  expect_equal(rownames(res), c("s1", "s2", "s3"))
  expect_equal(colnames(res), c("HOST", "COUNTRY", "ANNEE", "MOIS"))
  expect_true(all(vapply(res, is.factor, logical(1))))
  expect_equal(as.character(res$HOST), c("pig", "unknown", "cattle"))
  expect_equal(as.character(res$ANNEE), c("2020", "2021", "2021"))
  expect_equal(as.character(res$MOIS), c("01", "03", "12"))
  expect_silent(suppressMessages(prepare_input(raw, col_select = 2:4, id = 1, date = 3)))
  res_year <- suppressMessages(prepare_input(raw, col_select = 2:4, id = 1, date = 3))
  expect_equal(colnames(res_year), c("HOST", "COUNTRY", "ANNEE"))
})

test_that("prepare_input accepts column names", {
  raw <- data.frame(
    ID = c("s1", "s2", "s3"),
    HOST = c("pig", NA, "cattle"),
    DATE = c("09/01/2020", "15/03/2021", "30/12/2021"),
    COUNTRY = c("FR", "FR", "IT")
  )
  by_position <- suppressMessages(
    prepare_input(raw, col_select = c(2, 4), id = 1, date = 3, month = TRUE)
  )
  by_name <- suppressMessages(
    prepare_input(raw, col_select = c("HOST", "COUNTRY"), id = "ID", date = "DATE",
                  month = TRUE)
  )
  expect_identical(by_name, by_position)
  expect_error(prepare_input(raw, col_select = c("HOST", "SPECIES"), id = "ID"),
               "unknown column\\(s\\) in `col_select`: SPECIES")
  expect_error(prepare_input(raw, id = "STRAIN"), "unknown column\\(s\\) in `id`")
  expect_error(prepare_input(raw, col_select = 2:9), "between 1 and 4")
})

test_that("prepare_input reads dates in other formats and handles bad dates", {
  raw <- data.frame(
    ID = c("s1", "s2", "s3"),
    DATE = c("2020-01-09", NA, "2021-12-30")
  )
  res <- suppressMessages(
    prepare_input(raw, id = "ID", date = "DATE", month = TRUE, date_format = "%Y-%m-%d")
  )
  expect_equal(as.character(res$ANNEE), c("2020", "unknown", "2021"))
  expect_equal(as.character(res$MOIS), c("01", "unknown", "12"))
  # Date class is used as is
  raw$DATE <- as.Date(raw$DATE)
  res_date <- suppressMessages(prepare_input(raw, id = "ID", date = "DATE", month = TRUE))
  expect_identical(res_date, res)
  # a wrong format gives a warning
  raw$DATE <- c("2020-01-09", "2021-03-15", "2021-12-30")
  expect_warning(suppressMessages(prepare_input(raw, id = "ID", date = "DATE")),
                 "date_format")
  # date = 0 means no date: DATE is then kept as an ordinary metadata
  res0 <- suppressMessages(prepare_input(raw, id = "ID", date = 0))
  expect_equal(colnames(res0), "DATE")
})

test_that("prepare_input drops the identifier column by default", {
  raw <- data.frame(ID = c("s1", "s2"), HOST = c("pig", "cattle"))
  res <- suppressMessages(prepare_input(raw))
  expect_equal(colnames(res), "HOST")
})

test_that("prepare_input still accepts the deprecated m and a arguments", {
  raw <- data.frame(ID = c("s1", "s2"), DATE = c("09/01/2020", "15/03/2021"))
  expect_warning(
    res <- suppressMessages(prepare_input(raw, id = 1, date = 2, m = TRUE, a = FALSE)),
    "deprecated"
  )
  expect_equal(colnames(res), "MOIS")
})
```

# Clustering method

The clustering method uses three functions: `assess_gower()`,
`cstats_table()` and `select_silhouette()`. `cstats_table()` is optional when
the number of strains to sequence is fixed in advance.

## Distances and tree: assess_gower

`assess_gower()` computes a dissimilarity matrix between strains using the
Gower distance, which is suited to categorical metadata. Weights can be given
to the metadata to adjust their importance in the clustering. A hierarchical
clustering with complete linkage is then performed on this matrix, and the
dendrogram is drawn when `graph = TRUE`.

```{r function-assess_gower}
#' Compute Gower distances and the hierarchical clustering tree
#'
#' Computes the Gower dissimilarity between strains (suited to categorical
#' metadata) and performs an agglomerative hierarchical clustering with
#' complete linkage.
#'
#' @param clean_data A data frame of factors, one row per strain, as returned
#'   by [prepare_input()].
#' @param weights Numeric vector of weights, one per column of `clean_data`,
#'   to give more or less importance to each metadata. Defaults to equal
#'   weights.
#' @param graph If `TRUE` (default), the dendrogram is plotted.
#'
#' @return A list with two components:
#'   \describe{
#'     \item{gower_dist}{the Gower dissimilarity matrix, an object of class
#'       `dissimilarity` / `dist` (see [cluster::daisy()]);}
#'     \item{aggl.clust.c}{the clustering tree, an object of class `hclust`.}
#'   }
#' @source Adapted from the dissimilarity matrix and agglomerative clustering
#'   steps of Anastasia Reusova's tutorial:
#'   Reusova A. (2018). *Hierarchical Clustering on Categorical Data in R*.
#'   Towards Data Science.
#'   <https://medium.com/@anastasia.reusova/hierarchical-clustering-on-categorical-data-in-r-a27e578f2995>.
#'   Code: <https://github.com/khunreus/cluster-categorical>.
#' @export
#' @family clustering method
#' @importFrom cluster daisy
#' @importFrom stats hclust
#'
#' @examples
assess_gower <- function(clean_data, weights = rep.int(1, p), graph = TRUE){
  p=length(clean_data)
  gower_dist <- daisy(clean_data, metric = "gower", weights = weights)
  aggl.clust.c <- hclust(gower_dist, method = "complete")
  if (graph) {
    plot(aggl.clust.c,main = "Agglomerative, complete linkages")
  }
  return(list(gower_dist=gower_dist, aggl.clust.c=aggl.clust.c))
}
```

```{r examples-assess_gower}
raw_data <- salmonella_strains
prepared_data <- prepare_input(raw_data, col_select = c("CONTEXTE", "MATRICE1", "REGION", "SECTEUR", "LIEUPVT"),
                               id = "IDENTIFIANT", date = "DATE_PRELEVEMENT")
gower <- assess_gower(prepared_data, graph = TRUE)
```

```{r tests-assess_gower}
test_that("assess_gower returns a Gower distance and a complete-linkage tree", {
  clean_data <- data.frame(
    HOST = factor(c("pig", "pig", "cattle", "cattle")),
    COUNTRY = factor(c("FR", "FR", "FR", "IT")),
    row.names = c("s1", "s2", "s3", "s4")
  )
  res <- assess_gower(clean_data, graph = FALSE)
  expect_named(res, c("gower_dist", "aggl.clust.c"))
  expect_s3_class(res$gower_dist, "dist")
  expect_s3_class(res$aggl.clust.c, "hclust")
  d <- as.matrix(res$gower_dist)
  expect_equal(d["s1", "s2"], 0)
  expect_equal(d["s1", "s3"], 0.5)
  expect_equal(d["s1", "s4"], 1)
  weighted <- as.matrix(assess_gower(clean_data, weights = c(3, 1), graph = FALSE)$gower_dist)
  expect_equal(weighted["s1", "s3"], 0.75)
})
```

## Choosing the number of clusters: cstats_table

`cstats_table()` computes clustering statistics (see `fpc::cluster.stats()`)
for an increasing number of clusters: `step`, `2 * step`, ..., up to `k`. The
average silhouette width (`avg.silwidth`) is the most useful one: it is
plotted against the number of clusters, and the optimal number of clusters is
marked by a maximum or a plateau of the curve. The idea is to test a large
number of clusters without exceeding the number of strains that can be
sequenced; a larger `step` reduces the computing time.

```{r function-cstats_table}
#' Clustering statistics for an increasing number of clusters
#'
#' Cuts the clustering tree into `step`, `2 * step`, ..., `k` clusters and
#' computes, for each number of clusters, the statistics of
#' [fpc::cluster.stats()]. The average silhouette width can be plotted to help
#' choosing the number of clusters.
#'
#' @param dist A dissimilarity object, e.g. `gower_dist` returned by
#'   [assess_gower()].
#' @param tree An `hclust` object, e.g. `aggl.clust.c` returned by
#'   [assess_gower()].
#' @param k Largest number of clusters to test. Must be a multiple of `step`.
#' @param step Increment between two numbers of clusters tested.
#' @param graph_silhouette If `TRUE` (default), the average silhouette width
#'   is plotted against the number of clusters.
#' @param l Deprecated, use `step` instead.
#'
#' @return A data frame with one row per number of clusters tested (row names
#'   `Test <number of clusters>`) and the columns `cluster.number`, `n`,
#'   `within.cluster.ss`, `average.within`, `average.between`, `wb.ratio`,
#'   `dunn2`, `avg.silwidth` (see [fpc::cluster.stats()]), followed by
#'   cluster size columns. Values are rounded to 2 decimals.
#' @source Adapted from the `cstats.table()` function and the silhouette plot
#'   of Anastasia Reusova's tutorial:
#'   Reusova A. (2018). *Hierarchical Clustering on Categorical Data in R*.
#'   Towards Data Science.
#'   <https://medium.com/@anastasia.reusova/hierarchical-clustering-on-categorical-data-in-r-a27e578f2995>.
#'   Code: <https://github.com/khunreus/cluster-categorical>.
#' @export
#' @family clustering method
#' @importFrom fpc cluster.stats
#' @importFrom stats cutree
#' @importFrom ggplot2 ggplot aes .data geom_point geom_line ggtitle labs theme element_text
#'
#' @examples
cstats_table <- function(dist, tree, k, step, graph_silhouette = TRUE, l) {
   if (!missing(l)) {
     warning("`l` is deprecated, use `step` instead.", call. = FALSE)
     step <- l
   }
   l <- step
   if (k %% l != 0) {
     stop("k must be a multiple of step")
   }
   n=k/l
   clust.assess <- c("cluster.number","n","within.cluster.ss","average.within","average.between",
                     "wb.ratio","dunn2","avg.silwidth")
   clust.size <- c("cluster.size")
   stats.names <- c()
   row.clust <- c()
   output.stats <- matrix(ncol = n, nrow = length(clust.assess))
   cluster.sizes <- matrix(ncol =n, nrow = n)
   for(i in 1:n){
       row.clust[i] <- paste("Cluster-", i*l, " size")
   }
    for(i in 1:n){
     message("testing ", i*l, " clusters")
     stats.names[i] <- paste("Test", i*l)
     stats_i <- cluster.stats(d = dist, clustering = cutree(tree, k = i*l))

     for(j in seq_along(clust.assess)){
       output.stats[j, i] <- unlist(stats_i[clust.assess])[j]
     }

     for(d in 1:n) {
       cluster.sizes[d, i] <- unlist(stats_i[clust.size])[d*l]
     }
   }
   output.stats.df <- data.frame(output.stats)
   cluster.sizes <- data.frame(cluster.sizes)
   cluster.sizes[is.na(cluster.sizes)] <- 0
   rows.all <- c(clust.assess, row.clust)
   output <- rbind(output.stats.df, cluster.sizes)
   colnames(output) <- stats.names[1:n]
   rownames(output) <- rows.all
   is.num <- sapply(output, is.numeric)
   output[is.num] <- lapply(output[is.num], round, 2)
   data_fig <- data.frame(t(output))
   if (graph_silhouette){
     print(ggplot(data = data_fig,
            aes(x=.data$cluster.number, y=.data$avg.silwidth)) +
       geom_point()+
       geom_line()+
       ggtitle("Agglomerative clustering") +
       labs(x = "Num.of clusters", y = "Average silhouette width") +
       theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)))
   }
   data_fig
 }
```

```{r examples-cstats_table}
raw_data <- salmonella_strains
prepared_data <- prepare_input(raw_data, col_select = c("CONTEXTE", "MATRICE1", "REGION", "SECTEUR", "LIEUPVT"),
                               id = "IDENTIFIANT", date = "DATE_PRELEVEMENT")
gower <- assess_gower(prepared_data, graph = FALSE)
stats <- cstats_table(dist = gower$gower_dist, tree = gower$aggl.clust.c,
                      k = 60, step = 2)
```

With a small step (here every 2 clusters), the curve shows two plateaus. The
average silhouette width jumps to about 0.45 at 16 clusters and then stays
between 0.39 and 0.43 up to 30 clusters: **about 15 clusters** is a first
level that already captures the main structure of the collection. It jumps
again to about 0.47 at 34 clusters and stays between 0.47 and 0.51 up to 52
clusters: **about 33 clusters** is a second, finer level. Beyond, the
curve increases up to the number of distinct profiles (61), where every
profile is isolated: with categorical metadata, this maximum is not a natural
level of grouping. The number of strains to sequence can be chosen at one of
the two plateaus, depending on the resources available.

```{r tests-cstats_table}
test_that("cstats_table returns the cluster stats table", {
  raw_data <- salmonella_strains
  prepared_data <- suppressMessages(
    prepare_input(raw_data, col_select = c("CONTEXTE", "MATRICE1", "REGION", "SECTEUR", "LIEUPVT"),
                  id = "IDENTIFIANT", date = "DATE_PRELEVEMENT")
  )
  gower <- assess_gower(prepared_data, graph = FALSE)
  expect_message(
    stats <- cstats_table(gower$gower_dist, gower$aggl.clust.c, k = 30, step = 10,
                          graph_silhouette = FALSE),
    "testing 10 clusters"
  )
  expect_s3_class(stats, "data.frame")
  expect_equal(nrow(stats), 3)
  expect_equal(stats$cluster.number, c(10, 20, 30))
  expect_true(all(stats$avg.silwidth >= -1 & stats$avg.silwidth <= 1))
  expect_error(cstats_table(gower$gower_dist, gower$aggl.clust.c, k = 25, step = 10),
               "multiple")
  expect_warning(
    old_style <- suppressMessages(
      cstats_table(gower$gower_dist, gower$aggl.clust.c, k = 30, l = 10,
                   graph_silhouette = FALSE)
    ),
    "deprecated"
  )
  expect_identical(old_style, stats)
})
```

## Selecting the strains: select_silhouette

The last step selects one strain to sequence in each cluster. The number of
clusters `k` is either chosen from the silhouette plot or set to the number of
strains that can be sequenced. For each cluster, the strain with the largest
silhouette width — i.e. the best clustered strain — is selected. When several
strains share the largest silhouette width in a cluster, one of them is chosen
at random; use `seed` to make this choice reproducible.

```{r function-select_silhouette}
#' Select the best clustered strain of each cluster
#'
#' Cuts the strains into `k` clusters with [factoextra::hcut()] and selects,
#' in each cluster, the strain with the largest silhouette width. When several
#' strains share the largest silhouette width, one of them is chosen at
#' random.
#'
#' @param prepared_data A data frame with one row per strain, as returned by
#'   [prepare_input()]. Its rows must be in the same order as in `dist`.
#' @param dist A dissimilarity object, e.g. `gower_dist` returned by
#'   [assess_gower()].
#' @param k Number of clusters, i.e. number of strains to select. Must be
#'   between 2 and the number of strains minus 1.
#' @param isdiss Logical, whether `dist` is a dissimilarity object (default:
#'   `TRUE` when `dist` inherits from `"dist"`).
#' @param hc_func Hierarchical clustering function passed to
#'   [factoextra::hcut()]: `"hclust"` (default), `"agnes"` or `"diana"`.
#' @param hc_method Agglomeration method passed to [factoextra::hcut()],
#'   `"complete"` by default.
#' @param seed An integer passed to [set.seed()] to make the choice between
#'   ex aequo strains reproducible, or `NULL` (default) to leave the random
#'   number generator untouched.
#'
#' @return `prepared_data` with three additional columns:
#'   \describe{
#'     \item{cluster}{the cluster of the strain;}
#'     \item{size}{the number of strains in this cluster;}
#'     \item{selected}{the identifier of the strain selected for this
#'       cluster.}
#'   }
#'   The selected strains are given by `unique(result$selected)`.
#' @export
#' @family clustering method
#' @importFrom factoextra hcut
#'
#' @examples
select_silhouette <- function (prepared_data, dist, k, isdiss = inherits(dist, "dist"),
                               hc_func = "hclust", hc_method = "complete", seed = NULL) {
  n <- nrow(prepared_data)
  if (k < 2 || k >= n) {
    stop("k must be between 2 and the number of strains minus 1")
  }
  if (!is.null(seed)) {
    set.seed(seed)
  }
  clust2 <- hcut(dist, k, isdiss, hc_func, hc_method)
  widths <- clust2$silinfo$widths
  selection <- vapply(seq_len(k), function(i) {
    widths_i <- widths[widths$cluster == i, , drop = FALSE]
    best <- rownames(widths_i)[widths_i$sil_width == max(widths_i$sil_width)]
    if (length(best) > 1) {
      best <- best[sample.int(length(best), 1)]
    }
    best
  }, character(1))
  selected_data <- prepared_data
  selected_data$cluster <- unname(clust2$cluster)
  selected_data$size <- clust2$size[clust2$cluster]
  selected_data$selected <- selection[clust2$cluster]
  selected_data
}
```

```{r examples-select_silhouette}
raw_data <- salmonella_strains
prepared_data <- prepare_input(raw_data, col_select = c("CONTEXTE", "MATRICE1", "REGION", "SECTEUR", "LIEUPVT"),
                               id = "IDENTIFIANT", date = "DATE_PRELEVEMENT")
gower <- assess_gower(prepared_data, graph = FALSE)
selection <- select_silhouette(prepared_data, dist = gower$gower_dist, k = 20,
                               seed = 1)
# the 20 strains to sequence
unique(selection$selected)
```

```{r tests-select_silhouette}
test_that("select_silhouette selects one strain per cluster without global objects", {
  raw_data <- salmonella_strains
  prepared_data <- suppressMessages(
    prepare_input(raw_data, col_select = c("CONTEXTE", "MATRICE1", "REGION", "SECTEUR", "LIEUPVT"),
                  id = "IDENTIFIANT", date = "DATE_PRELEVEMENT")
  )
  dist <- assess_gower(prepared_data, graph = FALSE)$gower_dist
  selected <- select_silhouette(prepared_data, dist, k = 10)
  expect_equal(nrow(selected), nrow(prepared_data))
  expect_true(all(c("cluster", "size", "selected") %in% colnames(selected)))
  expect_equal(length(unique(selected$selected)), 10)
  # each selected strain belongs to the cluster it represents
  expect_equal(selected[selected$selected, "cluster"], selected$cluster)
  # size is the number of strains in the cluster
  expect_equal(selected$size, as.vector(table(selected$cluster)[as.character(selected$cluster)]))
})

test_that("select_silhouette is reproducible with seed and checks k", {
  raw_data <- salmonella_strains
  prepared_data <- suppressMessages(
    prepare_input(raw_data, col_select = c("CONTEXTE", "MATRICE1", "REGION", "SECTEUR", "LIEUPVT"),
                  id = "IDENTIFIANT", date = "DATE_PRELEVEMENT")
  )
  dist <- assess_gower(prepared_data, graph = FALSE)$gower_dist
  expect_identical(select_silhouette(prepared_data, dist, k = 20, seed = 42),
                   select_silhouette(prepared_data, dist, k = 20, seed = 42))
  expect_error(select_silhouette(prepared_data, dist, k = 1), "k must be")
  expect_error(select_silhouette(prepared_data, dist, k = nrow(prepared_data)), "k must be")
})
```

# Selecting strains for a sequencing budget: select_strains

`select_strains()` runs the whole clustering method in one step and answers
the practical question "*I can sequence at most `n_max` strains: which ones?*".

1. It computes the Gower distances and the clustering tree (as
   `assess_gower()`), then the average silhouette width for every number of
   clusters from 2 to the number of distinct profiles. The number of clusters
   with the largest average silhouette width is the **optimal number of
   clusters** `k_opt`.
2. It selects the strains according to the budget `n_max`:
   - no budget (`n_max = NULL`): one strain per optimal cluster, i.e. `k_opt`
     strains, with the status `"optimal"`;
   - budget larger than the optimum (`n_max >= k_opt`): the `k_opt` optimal
     strains, completed up to `n_max` strains (status `"supplementary"`) by
     cutting the tree into `n_max` clusters. Use `fill = FALSE` to stop at the
     optimum. As the clusters are nested, each supplementary strain comes from
     a cluster that does not contain an optimal strain yet;
   - budget smaller than the optimum (`n_max < k_opt`): the tree is cut into
     `n_max` clusters and one strain is selected in each (status
     `"selected"`). The optimal groups that are not represented by any
     selected strain are listed, so that the user knows what is missed.

In each cluster, the selected strain is the one with the largest silhouette
width, i.e. the best clustered one (ties are broken at random, use `seed` for
reproducibility).

With categorical metadata and equal weights, identical strains are at
distance 0 and the optimum is often close to the number of distinct profiles:
supplementary strains then mostly have the same metadata as already selected
strains, and add replicates rather than diversity. This is not a general
rule. The weights change the Gower distances between different strains, hence
the tree, the silhouette curve and the optimum (in the example of this
vignette, a weight of 3 on `REGION` lowers the optimum from 61 to 22
clusters), and supplementary strains can then add new profiles. Conversely,
below the optimum, the strains of a cluster are similar but not identical.
The report written by `report_selection()` gives, for the actual data, the
number of supplementary strains that have the same metadata as an already
selected strain, and how much the strains differ from the selected strain of
their cluster.

`select_strains(method = "profile")` applies the same logic to the profile
method. The strains with identical metadata form groups, sorted by decreasing
size (groups of the same size in random order); one strain per group is the
optimal selection:

- budget smaller than the number of groups: one strain in each of the `n_max`
  largest groups — the most frequent profiles are favoured, and the smallest
  groups (often strains with a unique profile) are listed as not represented;
- budget larger than the number of groups: one strain per group, then
  supplementary strains added turn by turn — a second strain in each group
  that has one, from the largest group to the smallest, then a third strain,
  and so on.

Within a group, the strains have the same metadata and are chosen at random
(use `seed` for reproducibility).

```{r function-select_strains}
#' Select strains to sequence, with or without a maximum number of strains
#'
#' Selects the strains to sequence with the clustering method or with the
#' profile method, taking into account the maximum number of strains that
#' can be sequenced.
#'
#' **Clustering method** (`method = "clustering"`, default): computes the
#' Gower distances and the hierarchical clustering tree, finds the optimal
#' number of clusters (largest average silhouette width) and selects in each
#' cluster the strain with the largest silhouette width.
#'
#' **Profile method** (`method = "profile"`): groups the strains with
#' identical metadata (distinct profiles) and sorts the groups by decreasing
#' size (ties in random order). One strain per group gives the "optimal"
#' selection. With a smaller `n_max`, one strain is selected in each of the
#' `n_max` largest groups. With a larger `n_max`, supplementary strains are
#' added turn by turn: a second strain in each group that has one, from the
#' largest group to the smallest, then a third strain, and so on. Strains of
#' a group have the same metadata, so the strain(s) of a group are chosen at
#' random.
#'
#' @param prepared_data A data frame with one row per strain, as returned by
#'   [prepare_input()].
#' @param n_max Maximum number of strains that can be sequenced, or `NULL`
#'   (default) to select the optimal number of strains (one per optimal
#'   cluster or one per distinct profile).
#' @param method `"clustering"` (default) or `"profile"`.
#' @param fill If `TRUE` (default) and `n_max` is larger than the optimal
#'   number of strains, the selection is completed up to `n_max` strains
#'   with supplementary strains. If `FALSE`, the selection stops at the
#'   optimum.
#' @param weights Clustering method only: numeric vector of weights, one per
#'   column of `prepared_data` (see [assess_gower()]), or `NULL` for equal
#'   weights.
#' @param k_max Clustering method only: largest number of clusters tested to
#'   find the optimum. By default, the number of distinct profiles (beyond
#'   it, clusters only split identical strains), limited to the number of
#'   strains minus 1. Lower it to save time on large datasets.
#' @param seed An integer passed to [set.seed()] to make the random choices
#'   reproducible (ex aequo strains or groups), or `NULL` (default).
#'
#' @return An object of class `strainselect_selection`, a list with:
#'   \describe{
#'     \item{table}{`prepared_data` with the columns `cluster` (cluster in
#'       the final cut of the tree, or group of identical strains numbered by
#'       decreasing size for the profile method), `optimal_group` (cluster at
#'       the optimal number of clusters, or group of identical strains),
#'       `selected` (`TRUE`/`FALSE`), `status` (`"optimal"`,
#'       `"supplementary"`, `"selected"` or `"not selected"`),
#'       `representative` (identifier of the selected strain of the same
#'       cluster or group, `NA` if none) and `group_represented` (whether the
#'       optimal group of the strain contains a selected strain);}
#'     \item{selected}{identifiers of the selected strains;}
#'     \item{method}{the method used;}
#'     \item{k_opt}{optimal number of strains: optimal number of clusters, or
#'       number of distinct profiles for the profile method;}
#'     \item{k}{number of selected strains;}
#'     \item{n_max, fill}{the arguments used;}
#'     \item{silhouette}{clustering method: data frame of the average
#'       silhouette width (`avg_silwidth`) for each number of clusters `k`
#'       tested;}
#'     \item{groups}{profile method: data frame with, for each group of
#'       identical strains, its `size`, its number of selected strains
#'       (`n_selected`) and its `profile`;}
#'     \item{unrepresented_groups}{optimal groups without any selected
#'       strain (only when `n_max` is smaller than the optimum);}
#'     \item{n_strains, n_profiles}{number of strains and of distinct
#'       profiles;}
#'     \item{weights}{the weights of the metadata (clustering method);}
#'     \item{gower}{the output of [assess_gower()] (clustering method).}
#'   }
#'   The object has `print()` and `plot()` methods, and can be exported with
#'   [export_selection()] or summarised in a report with
#'   [report_selection()].
#' @export
#' @family clustering method
#' @family profile method
#' @importFrom cluster silhouette
#' @importFrom stats cutree
#'
#' @examples
select_strains <- function(prepared_data, n_max = NULL,
                           method = c("clustering", "profile"), fill = TRUE,
                           weights = NULL, k_max = NULL, seed = NULL) {
  method <- match.arg(method)
  n <- nrow(prepared_data)
  n_profiles <- nrow(unique(prepared_data))
  if (n < 3 || n_profiles < 2) {
    stop("at least 3 strains and 2 distinct profiles are needed", call. = FALSE)
  }
  if (!is.null(n_max)) {
    if (!is.numeric(n_max) || length(n_max) != 1 || n_max < 1) {
      stop("`n_max` must be a positive number", call. = FALSE)
    }
    n_max <- as.integer(n_max)
    if (n_max > n) {
      message("n_max (", n_max, ") is larger than the number of strains: ",
              "all ", n, " strains are selected")
      n_max <- n
    }
  }
  if (!is.null(seed)) {
    set.seed(seed)
  }
  if (method == "profile") {
    return(select_by_profile(prepared_data, n_max, fill, n_profiles))
  }
  if (is.null(weights)) {
    weights <- rep.int(1, ncol(prepared_data))
  }
  gower <- assess_gower(prepared_data, weights = weights, graph = FALSE)
  dist <- gower$gower_dist
  tree <- gower$aggl.clust.c
  if (is.null(k_max)) {
    k_max <- n_profiles
  }
  k_max <- max(2, min(k_max, n - 1))
  ks <- 2:k_max
  avg_silwidth <- vapply(ks, function(k) {
    summary(silhouette(cutree(tree, k = k), dist))$avg.width
  }, numeric(1))
  k_opt <- ks[which.max(avg_silwidth)]

  optimal_group <- cutree(tree, k = k_opt)
  optimal <- best_strains(tree, dist, k_opt)
  if (is.null(n_max)) {
    k <- k_opt
  } else if (n_max >= k_opt) {
    k <- if (fill) n_max else k_opt
  } else {
    k <- n_max
  }
  cluster <- cutree(tree, k = k)
  if (k >= k_opt) {
    # clusters are nested: complete the optimal strains with one strain in
    # each cluster that does not contain an optimal strain yet
    missing_clusters <- setdiff(seq_len(k), cluster[optimal])
    supplementary <- unname(best_strains(tree, dist, k)[missing_clusters])
    selected <- c(optimal, supplementary)
    status <- ifelse(rownames(prepared_data) %in% optimal, "optimal",
                     ifelse(rownames(prepared_data) %in% supplementary,
                            "supplementary", "not selected"))
  } else {
    selected <- best_strains(tree, dist, k)
    status <- ifelse(rownames(prepared_data) %in% selected, "selected",
                     "not selected")
  }
  selected <- unname(selected)
  representative <- vapply(cluster, function(cl) {
    selected[cluster[selected] == cl][1]
  }, character(1))
  represented_groups <- unique(optimal_group[selected])

  table <- prepared_data
  table$cluster <- unname(cluster)
  table$optimal_group <- unname(optimal_group)
  table$selected <- rownames(prepared_data) %in% selected
  table$status <- status
  table$representative <- unname(representative)
  table$group_represented <- unname(optimal_group) %in% represented_groups

  structure(
    list(
      table = table,
      selected = selected,
      method = "clustering",
      k_opt = k_opt,
      k = k,
      n_max = n_max,
      fill = fill,
      silhouette = data.frame(k = ks, avg_silwidth = avg_silwidth),
      groups = NULL,
      unrepresented_groups = setdiff(seq_len(k_opt), represented_groups),
      n_strains = n,
      n_profiles = n_profiles,
      weights = weights,
      gower = gower
    ),
    class = "strainselect_selection"
  )
}

#' Selection with the profile method
#'
#' @param prepared_data,n_max,fill See [select_strains()].
#' @param n_profiles Number of distinct profiles.
#'
#' @return An object of class `strainselect_selection`.
#' @noRd
select_by_profile <- function(prepared_data, n_max, fill, n_profiles) {
  ids <- rownames(prepared_data)
  profile <- do.call(paste, c(lapply(prepared_data, as.character), sep = " | "))
  sizes <- table(profile)
  # groups numbered by decreasing size, ties in random order
  ord <- order(-as.vector(sizes), sample.int(length(sizes)))
  group_number <- stats::setNames(seq_along(ord), names(sizes)[ord])
  group <- unname(group_number[profile])
  n_groups <- length(sizes)
  # strains of a group in random order: the first one is chosen first
  members <- split(ids, factor(group, levels = seq_len(n_groups)))
  members <- lapply(members, function(m) m[sample.int(length(m))])

  if (is.null(n_max)) {
    k <- n_groups
  } else if (n_max >= n_groups) {
    k <- if (fill) n_max else n_groups
  } else {
    k <- n_max
  }
  first <- vapply(members, `[`, character(1), 1)
  if (k < n_groups) {
    selected <- unname(first[seq_len(k)])
    status <- ifelse(ids %in% selected, "selected", "not selected")
  } else {
    # one strain per group, then turn by turn from the largest group
    supplementary <- character(0)
    turn <- 2
    while (n_groups + length(supplementary) < k) {
      for (g in seq_len(n_groups)) {
        if (length(members[[g]]) >= turn && n_groups + length(supplementary) < k) {
          supplementary <- c(supplementary, members[[g]][turn])
        }
      }
      turn <- turn + 1
    }
    selected <- c(unname(first), supplementary)
    status <- ifelse(ids %in% first, "optimal",
                     ifelse(ids %in% supplementary, "supplementary",
                            "not selected"))
  }
  is_selected <- ids %in% selected
  represented_groups <- unique(group[is_selected])
  representative <- ifelse(group %in% represented_groups,
                           unname(first[group]), NA_character_)

  table <- prepared_data
  table$cluster <- group
  table$optimal_group <- group
  table$selected <- is_selected
  table$status <- status
  table$representative <- representative
  table$group_represented <- group %in% represented_groups

  groups <- data.frame(
    group = seq_len(n_groups),
    size = as.vector(sizes)[ord],
    n_selected = as.vector(table(factor(group[is_selected],
                                        levels = seq_len(n_groups)))),
    profile = names(sizes)[ord]
  )

  structure(
    list(
      table = table,
      selected = selected,
      method = "profile",
      k_opt = n_groups,
      k = length(selected),
      n_max = n_max,
      fill = fill,
      silhouette = NULL,
      groups = groups,
      unrepresented_groups = setdiff(seq_len(n_groups), represented_groups),
      n_strains = nrow(prepared_data),
      n_profiles = n_profiles,
      weights = NULL,
      gower = NULL
    ),
    class = "strainselect_selection"
  )
}

#' Best clustered strain of each cluster
#'
#' @param tree An `hclust` object.
#' @param dist The dissimilarity object used to build `tree`.
#' @param k Number of clusters.
#'
#' @return A character vector with, for each cluster `1:k`, the identifier of
#'   the strain with the largest silhouette width (ties broken at random).
#' @noRd
best_strains <- function(tree, dist, k) {
  ids <- attr(dist, "Labels")
  cluster <- cutree(tree, k = k)
  if (k >= length(ids)) {
    return(ids[order(cluster)])
  }
  sil_width <- silhouette(cluster, dist)[, "sil_width"]
  vapply(seq_len(k), function(i) {
    in_cluster <- which(cluster == i)
    best <- in_cluster[sil_width[in_cluster] == max(sil_width[in_cluster])]
    if (length(best) > 1) {
      best <- best[sample.int(length(best), 1)]
    }
    ids[best]
  }, character(1))
}

#' @export
print.strainselect_selection <- function(x, ...) {
  profile <- identical(x$method, "profile")
  cat("Strain selection (", if (profile) "profile" else "clustering",
      " method)\n", sep = "")
  cat("  strains:", x$n_strains, "- distinct profiles:", x$n_profiles, "\n")
  if (profile) {
    cat("  groups of identical strains:", x$k_opt, "\n")
  } else {
    cat("  optimal number of clusters (k_opt):", x$k_opt, "\n")
  }
  if (is.null(x$n_max)) {
    cat("  maximum number of strains (n_max): not given\n")
  } else {
    cat("  maximum number of strains (n_max):", x$n_max, "\n")
  }
  status <- table(factor(x$table$status[x$table$selected],
                         levels = c("optimal", "supplementary", "selected")))
  status <- status[status > 0]
  cat("  selected strains:", length(x$selected),
      paste0("(", paste(names(status), status, sep = ": ", collapse = ", "), ")"),
      "\n")
  if (!is.null(x$n_max) && x$n_max > x$k_opt && !x$fill) {
    cat("  the selection stops at the optimum:", x$n_max - x$k_opt,
        "strains of the budget are not used (fill = FALSE)\n")
  }
  if (length(x$unrepresented_groups) > 0) {
    cat(if (profile) "  groups not represented:" else "  optimal groups not represented:",
        length(x$unrepresented_groups), "out of", x$k_opt, "\n")
  }
  invisible(x)
}

#' @export
#' @importFrom ggplot2 ggplot aes .data geom_point geom_line geom_vline geom_col annotate labs
plot.strainselect_selection <- function(x, ...) {
  if (identical(x$method, "profile")) {
    p <- ggplot(x$groups, aes(x = .data$group)) +
      geom_col(aes(y = .data$size), fill = "grey80") +
      geom_col(aes(y = .data$n_selected), fill = "steelblue") +
      labs(x = "Group of identical strains (by decreasing size)",
           y = "Number of strains",
           title = "Selected strains (blue) in each group (grey)")
    if (!is.null(x$n_max) && x$n_max < x$k_opt) {
      p <- p +
        geom_vline(xintercept = x$n_max + 0.5, linetype = "dotted",
                   colour = "firebrick") +
        annotate("text", x = x$n_max + 0.5, y = max(x$groups$size),
                 label = paste("n_max =", x$n_max), colour = "firebrick",
                 hjust = -0.1, vjust = 1)
    }
    return(p)
  }
  p <- ggplot(x$silhouette, aes(x = .data$k, y = .data$avg_silwidth)) +
    geom_line() +
    geom_point() +
    geom_vline(xintercept = x$k_opt, linetype = "dashed", colour = "darkgreen") +
    annotate("text", x = x$k_opt, y = min(x$silhouette$avg_silwidth),
             label = paste("k_opt =", x$k_opt), colour = "darkgreen",
             hjust = 1.1, vjust = 0) +
    labs(x = "Number of clusters", y = "Average silhouette width",
         title = "Choice of the number of strains")
  if (!is.null(x$n_max)) {
    p <- p +
      geom_vline(xintercept = x$n_max, linetype = "dotted", colour = "firebrick") +
      annotate("text", x = x$n_max, y = max(x$silhouette$avg_silwidth),
               label = paste("n_max =", x$n_max), colour = "firebrick",
               hjust = -0.1, vjust = 1)
  }
  p
}
```

```{r examples-select_strains}
prepared_data <- prepare_input(
  salmonella_strains,
  col_select = c("CONTEXTE", "MATRICE1", "REGION", "SECTEUR", "LIEUPVT"),
  id = "IDENTIFIANT", date = "DATE_PRELEVEMENT"
)
# clustering method, no budget: optimal number of strains
res <- select_strains(prepared_data, seed = 1)
res
plot(res)
# budget smaller than the optimum
res_20 <- select_strains(prepared_data, n_max = 20, seed = 1)
res_20
head(res_20$table[, c("cluster", "optimal_group", "selected", "status")])
# profile method, budget larger than the number of distinct profiles
res_profile <- select_strains(prepared_data, n_max = 75, method = "profile", seed = 1)
res_profile
plot(res_profile)
head(res_profile$groups)
# profile method, budget smaller than the number of distinct profiles:
# one strain in each of the 20 largest groups
res_profile_20 <- select_strains(prepared_data, n_max = 20, method = "profile", seed = 1)
plot(res_profile_20)
```

```{r tests-select_strains}
prepared_test <- function() {
  suppressMessages(prepare_input(
    salmonella_strains,
    col_select = c("CONTEXTE", "MATRICE1", "REGION", "SECTEUR", "LIEUPVT"),
    id = "IDENTIFIANT", date = "DATE_PRELEVEMENT"
  ))
}

test_that("select_strains selects the optimal number of strains by default", {
  pd <- prepared_test()
  res <- select_strains(pd, seed = 1)
  expect_s3_class(res, "strainselect_selection")
  expect_equal(res$method, "clustering")
  expect_equal(res$k_opt, res$silhouette$k[which.max(res$silhouette$avg_silwidth)])
  expect_equal(length(res$selected), res$k_opt)
  expect_true(all(res$table$status[res$table$selected] == "optimal"))
  # one selected strain per cluster, which represents its cluster
  expect_equal(sort(unique(res$table$cluster[res$table$selected])), seq_len(res$k_opt))
  expect_equal(res$table[res$table$representative, "cluster"], res$table$cluster)
  expect_length(res$unrepresented_groups, 0)
  expect_output(print(res), "optimal number of clusters")
  expect_s3_class(plot(res), "ggplot")
})

test_that("select_strains completes the selection up to n_max", {
  pd <- prepared_test()
  opt <- select_strains(pd, seed = 1)
  n_max <- opt$k_opt + 10
  res <- select_strains(pd, n_max = n_max, seed = 1)
  expect_equal(length(res$selected), n_max)
  expect_equal(sum(res$table$status == "optimal"), opt$k_opt)
  expect_equal(sum(res$table$status == "supplementary"), 10)
  # the optimal strains are those of the selection without budget
  expect_setequal(rownames(res$table)[res$table$status == "optimal"], opt$selected)
  expect_equal(sort(unique(res$table$cluster[res$table$selected])), seq_len(n_max))
  # fill = FALSE stops at the optimum
  res_nofill <- select_strains(pd, n_max = n_max, fill = FALSE, seed = 1)
  expect_equal(length(res_nofill$selected), opt$k_opt)
  expect_output(print(res_nofill), "not used")
})

test_that("select_strains respects a budget smaller than the optimum", {
  pd <- prepared_test()
  res <- select_strains(pd, n_max = 20, seed = 1)
  expect_equal(length(res$selected), 20)
  expect_true(all(res$table$status[res$table$selected] == "selected"))
  expect_equal(sort(unique(res$table$cluster[res$table$selected])), 1:20)
  # unrepresented optimal groups are reported
  expect_equal(length(res$unrepresented_groups), res$k_opt - 20)
  expect_false(any(res$table$group_represented[
    res$table$optimal_group %in% res$unrepresented_groups]))
  expect_output(print(res), "not represented")
})

test_that("select_strains checks its arguments and is reproducible", {
  pd <- prepared_test()
  expect_identical(select_strains(pd, n_max = 30, seed = 3)$selected,
                   select_strains(pd, n_max = 30, seed = 3)$selected)
  expect_error(select_strains(pd, n_max = 0), "positive")
  expect_message(res <- select_strains(pd, n_max = 500), "all 100 strains")
  expect_equal(length(res$selected), 100)
  expect_error(select_strains(pd[1:2, ]), "at least 3 strains")
  expect_error(select_strains(pd, method = "other"))
})

test_that("profile method: one strain per distinct profile by default", {
  pd <- prepared_test()
  res <- select_strains(pd, method = "profile", seed = 1)
  n_profiles <- nrow(unique(pd))
  expect_equal(res$method, "profile")
  expect_equal(res$k_opt, n_profiles)
  expect_equal(length(res$selected), n_profiles)
  expect_true(all(res$table$status[res$table$selected] == "optimal"))
  expect_true(all(res$groups$n_selected == 1))
  # groups are numbered by decreasing size
  expect_false(is.unsorted(rev(res$groups$size)))
  expect_equal(res$groups$size, as.vector(table(res$table$cluster)))
  # strains of a group have the same profile
  profiles <- do.call(paste, lapply(pd, as.character))
  expect_true(all(tapply(profiles, res$table$cluster, function(p) length(unique(p))) == 1))
  expect_output(print(res), "profile method")
  expect_s3_class(plot(res), "ggplot")
})

test_that("profile method: largest groups first when n_max is smaller", {
  pd <- prepared_test()
  res <- select_strains(pd, n_max = 20, method = "profile", seed = 1)
  expect_equal(length(res$selected), 20)
  expect_true(all(res$table$status[res$table$selected] == "selected"))
  expect_equal(res$groups$n_selected, rep(c(1, 0), c(20, res$k_opt - 20)))
  expect_equal(res$unrepresented_groups, 21:res$k_opt)
  # the selected groups are at least as large as the others
  expect_gte(min(res$groups$size[1:20]), max(res$groups$size[-(1:20)]))
  expect_true(all(is.na(res$table$representative[!res$table$group_represented])))
  expect_output(print(res), "groups not represented")
})

test_that("profile method: supplementary strains turn by turn", {
  pd <- prepared_test()
  res <- select_strains(pd, n_max = 75, method = "profile", seed = 1)
  n_groups <- res$k_opt
  extra <- 75 - n_groups
  expect_equal(length(res$selected), 75)
  expect_equal(sum(res$table$status == "optimal"), n_groups)
  expect_equal(sum(res$table$status == "supplementary"), extra)
  # second turn: one more strain in the largest groups that have one
  can_have_2 <- which(res$groups$size >= 2)
  expected <- pmin(res$groups$size, 1)
  expected[can_have_2[seq_len(min(extra, length(can_have_2)))]] <- 2
  if (extra <= length(can_have_2)) {
    expect_equal(res$groups$n_selected, expected)
  }
  # all strains when n_max = number of strains; fill = FALSE stops at the profiles
  expect_equal(length(select_strains(pd, n_max = 100, method = "profile")$selected), 100)
  expect_equal(length(select_strains(pd, n_max = 75, method = "profile",
                                     fill = FALSE)$selected), n_groups)
  expect_identical(select_strains(pd, n_max = 30, method = "profile", seed = 2)$selected,
                   select_strains(pd, n_max = 30, method = "profile", seed = 2)$selected)
})
```

## Exporting the result: export_selection

`export_selection()` returns — and optionally writes to a CSV file — the
original metadata table with the columns added by `select_strains()`. The file
can be opened in a spreadsheet and filtered on `selected` to get the list of
strains to sequence.

```{r function-export_selection}
#' Export the strain selection with the original metadata
#'
#' Adds the results of [select_strains()] (`cluster`, `optimal_group`,
#' `selected`, `status`, `representative`, `group_represented`) to the
#' original metadata table and optionally writes it to a CSV file.
#'
#' @param x An object returned by [select_strains()].
#' @param data The original metadata table (e.g. the table given to
#'   [prepare_input()]), or `NULL` to export only the metadata used for the
#'   selection.
#' @param id Name or position of the column of `data` containing the strain
#'   identifiers.
#' @param file Path of the CSV file to write, or `NULL` (default) to write
#'   nothing.
#' @param sep Field separator of the CSV file (`";"` by default).
#'
#' @return A data frame with one row per strain (in the order of `data`):
#'   the columns of `data` followed by the columns of the selection. It is
#'   returned invisibly when `file` is given.
#' @export
#' @family clustering method
#' @importFrom utils write.table
#'
#' @examples
export_selection <- function(x, data = NULL, id = 1, file = NULL, sep = ";") {
  if (!inherits(x, "strainselect_selection")) {
    stop("`x` must be the result of select_strains()", call. = FALSE)
  }
  added <- c("cluster", "optimal_group", "selected", "status",
             "representative", "group_represented")
  results <- x$table[, added]
  if (is.null(data)) {
    out <- data.frame(id = rownames(x$table),
                      x$table[, setdiff(names(x$table), added), drop = FALSE],
                      results, row.names = NULL, check.names = FALSE)
  } else {
    data <- as.data.frame(data)
    id <- column_position(data, id, "id")
    ids <- as.character(data[[id]])
    if (!all(rownames(x$table) %in% ids)) {
      stop("some strains of the selection are not in `data`; check `id`",
           call. = FALSE)
    }
    out <- data.frame(data, results[match(ids, rownames(results)), ],
                      row.names = NULL, check.names = FALSE)
  }
  if (!is.null(file)) {
    write.table(out, file = file, sep = sep, row.names = FALSE,
                fileEncoding = "UTF-8")
    message("selection written to ", file)
    return(invisible(out))
  }
  out
}
```

```{r examples-export_selection}
prepared_data <- prepare_input(
  salmonella_strains,
  col_select = c("CONTEXTE", "MATRICE1", "REGION", "SECTEUR", "LIEUPVT"),
  id = "IDENTIFIANT", date = "DATE_PRELEVEMENT"
)
res <- select_strains(prepared_data, n_max = 20, seed = 1)
selection <- export_selection(res, data = salmonella_strains, id = "IDENTIFIANT")
# the strains to sequence, with all their metadata
head(selection[selection$selected, c("IDENTIFIANT", "REGION", "status")])
# write the table to a CSV file
export_selection(res, data = salmonella_strains, id = "IDENTIFIANT",
                 file = file.path(tempdir(), "selection.csv"))
```

```{r tests-export_selection}
test_that("export_selection adds the selection to the original metadata", {
  pd <- suppressMessages(prepare_input(
    salmonella_strains, col_select = c("CONTEXTE", "REGION", "SECTEUR"),
    id = "IDENTIFIANT"
  ))
  res <- select_strains(pd, n_max = 15, seed = 1)
  out <- export_selection(res, data = salmonella_strains, id = "IDENTIFIANT")
  expect_equal(nrow(out), nrow(salmonella_strains))
  expect_equal(out$IDENTIFIANT, salmonella_strains$IDENTIFIANT)
  expect_equal(ncol(out), ncol(salmonella_strains) + 6)
  expect_equal(sum(out$selected), 15)
  expect_setequal(out$IDENTIFIANT[out$selected], res$selected)
  # without data: only the metadata used for the selection
  out_small <- export_selection(res)
  expect_equal(names(out_small)[1:4], c("id", "CONTEXTE", "REGION", "SECTEUR"))
  # CSV file
  file <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv")
  expect_message(export_selection(res, salmonella_strains, "IDENTIFIANT", file = file),
                 "written")
  back <- read.csv(file, sep = ";", encoding = "UTF-8")
  expect_equal(nrow(back), 100)
  expect_equal(sum(back$selected), 15)
  expect_error(export_selection(list()), "select_strains")
  expect_error(export_selection(res, salmonella_strains, id = "REGION"), "check `id`")
})
```

## Reporting: report_selection

`report_selection()` writes an HTML report of the selection: the parameters,
the silhouette curve with the optimum and the budget, the list of the
selected strains, the optimal groups that are not represented and the size of
each cluster. Together with the CSV file of `export_selection()`, it documents
the choice of the strains to sequence.

```{r function-report_selection}
#' Write an HTML report of the strain selection
#'
#' Renders an HTML report of a selection made with [select_strains()]:
#' parameters and summary, silhouette curve with the optimal number of
#' clusters and the maximum number of strains, list of the selected strains
#' (with their metadata), optimal groups that are not represented, sizes of
#' the clusters and description of the columns of the CSV file (which ones
#' were used for the selection). Requires the {rmarkdown} package and pandoc.
#'
#' @param x An object returned by [select_strains()].
#' @param file Path of the HTML file to write.
#' @param data The original metadata table, or `NULL` to show only the
#'   metadata used for the selection (see [export_selection()]).
#' @param id Name or position of the column of `data` containing the strain
#'   identifiers.
#' @param title Title of the report.
#' @param csv If `TRUE` (default), the table of [export_selection()] is also
#'   written as a CSV file next to the report (same name, `.csv` extension).
#'
#' @return The path of the HTML report, invisibly.
#' @export
#' @family clustering method
#'
#' @examples
report_selection <- function(x, file = "strain_selection_report.html",
                             data = NULL, id = 1,
                             title = "Selection of strains to sequence",
                             csv = TRUE) {
  if (!inherits(x, "strainselect_selection")) {
    stop("`x` must be the result of select_strains()", call. = FALSE)
  }
  if (!requireNamespace("rmarkdown", quietly = TRUE)) {
    stop("the rmarkdown package is needed to write the report", call. = FALSE)
  }
  table <- export_selection(x, data = data, id = id)
  id_column <- if (is.null(data)) "id" else names(table)[column_position(data, id, "id")]
  if (csv) {
    csv_file <- sub("\\.html?$", "", file)
    csv_file <- paste0(csv_file, ".csv")
    export_selection(x, data = data, id = id, file = csv_file)
  }
  template <- system.file("rmarkdown", "selection_report.Rmd",
                          package = "strainselect")
  out_dir <- dirname(normalizePath(file, mustWork = FALSE))
  dir.create(out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
  work_dir <- tempfile("strainselect_report")
  dir.create(work_dir)
  rmd <- file.path(work_dir, "selection_report.Rmd")
  file.copy(template, rmd)
  # the report may be rendered inside another document (e.g. a vignette)
  old_options <- options(knitr.duplicate.label = "allow")
  on.exit(options(old_options), add = TRUE)
  rmarkdown::render(
    rmd,
    output_file = basename(file),
    output_dir = out_dir,
    intermediates_dir = work_dir,
    params = list(selection = x, table = table, id_column = id_column,
                  title = title),
    envir = new.env(),
    quiet = TRUE
  )
  out <- file.path(out_dir, basename(file))
  message("report written to ", out)
  invisible(out)
}
```

```{r examples-report_selection}
prepared_data <- prepare_input(
  salmonella_strains,
  col_select = c("CONTEXTE", "MATRICE1", "REGION", "SECTEUR", "LIEUPVT"),
  id = "IDENTIFIANT", date = "DATE_PRELEVEMENT"
)
res <- select_strains(prepared_data, n_max = 20, seed = 1)
if (requireNamespace("rmarkdown", quietly = TRUE) && rmarkdown::pandoc_available()) {
  report_selection(res, file = file.path(tempdir(), "selection.html"),
                   data = salmonella_strains, id = "IDENTIFIANT")
}
```

  skip_if_not_installed("rmarkdown")

# Profile method

This method groups strains that are strictly identical for all the selected
metadata, and selects one strain per group. Unlike the clustering method, all
strains of a group are identical, and strains that are similar to no other
strain form a group on their own. It uses three functions: `prepare_upset()`,
`define_profiles()` and `select_profiles()`.

## Binary table: prepare_upset

`prepare_upset()` creates a binary table from the prepared data: there is one
column per modality of each metadata (named `<metadata> _ <modality>`), filled
with 1 if the strain has this modality and 0 otherwise.

```{r function-prepare_upset}
#' Build the binary table of metadata modalities
#'
#' Creates one column per modality of each metadata, filled with 1 when the
#' strain has this modality and 0 otherwise. The result can be used to draw an
#' UpSet plot (e.g. with `UpSetR::upset()`) and to define profiles with
#' [define_profiles()].
#'
#' @param prepared_data A data frame with one row per strain, as returned by
#'   [prepare_input()].
#'
#' @return A data frame with the same row names as `prepared_data` and one
#'   numeric (0/1) column per modality, named `"<metadata> _ <modality>"`.
#'   Modalities appear in their order of first appearance.
#' @export
#' @family profile method
#'
#' @examples
prepare_upset<- function(prepared_data){
  upset_data <- data.frame(row.names = rownames(prepared_data))
  metadata <- colnames(prepared_data)
  for (i in seq_along(prepared_data)){
    x <- as.character(prepared_data[[i]])
    vect <- unique(prepared_data[[i]])
    tab <- 1 * outer(x, as.character(vect), "==")
    tab[is.na(tab)] <- 0
    colnames(tab) <- paste(metadata[i], "_", vect)
    upset_data <- cbind(upset_data, tab)
  }
  upset_data
}

```

```{r examples-prepare_upset}
raw_data <- salmonella_strains
prepared_data <- prepare_input(raw_data, col_select = c("CONTEXTE", "MATRICE1", "REGION", "SECTEUR", "LIEUPVT"),
                               id = "IDENTIFIANT", date = "DATE_PRELEVEMENT")
upset_data <- prepare_upset(prepared_data)
upset_data[1:5, 1:4]
```

The binary table can be used to visualise the groups of identical strains in
an UpSet plot, for instance with the {UpSetR} package:

```{r upset-plot, eval = requireNamespace("UpSetR", quietly = TRUE), fig.width = 9, fig.height = 5}
# the 12 most frequent modalities
UpSetR::upset(upset_data, nsets = 12, order.by = "freq", nintersects = 20,
              mb.ratio = c(0.55, 0.45), text.scale = 1.1)
```

```{r tests-prepare_upset}
test_that("prepare_upset builds a binary table with one column per modality", {
  prepared_data <- data.frame(
    HOST = factor(c("pig", "cattle", "pig")),
    COUNTRY = factor(c("FR", "FR", "IT")),
    row.names = c("s1", "s2", "s3")
  )
  upset <- prepare_upset(prepared_data)
  expect_equal(rownames(upset), c("s1", "s2", "s3"))
  expect_equal(colnames(upset),
               c("HOST _ pig", "HOST _ cattle", "COUNTRY _ FR", "COUNTRY _ IT"))
  expect_equal(upset[["HOST _ pig"]], c(1, 0, 1))
  expect_equal(upset[["COUNTRY _ IT"]], c(0, 0, 1))
  # each strain has exactly one modality per metadata
  expect_true(all(rowSums(upset) == ncol(prepared_data)))
})
```

## Groups of identical strains: define_profiles

`define_profiles()` builds a profile for each strain by concatenating the
columns of the binary table. Strains with identical profiles are put in the
same group; a profile shared by no other strain forms a group with a single
strain.

```{r function-define_profiles}
#' Group strains with identical profiles
#'
#' Concatenates the columns of the binary table into one profile per strain
#' and gives the same group number to strains with identical profiles.
#'
#' @param data A data frame with one row per strain, typically the binary
#'   table returned by [prepare_upset()].
#' @param sep Separator used between values when building the profiles
#'   (none by default).
#'
#' @return A data frame with the same row names as `data` and three columns:
#'   \describe{
#'     \item{profiles}{the profile of the strain (concatenated values);}
#'     \item{group}{an integer identifying the group of identical profiles;}
#'     \item{names}{the strain identifier.}
#'   }
#' @export
#' @family profile method
#'
#' @examples
define_profiles <- function (data, sep = ""){
  profiles <- data.frame(profiles = do.call(paste, c(unname(as.list(data)), sep = sep)),
                         row.names = rownames(data))
  profiles$group <- as.integer(factor(profiles$profiles))
  profiles$names <- rownames(profiles)
  profiles
}
```

```{r examples-define_profiles}
raw_data <- salmonella_strains
prepared_data <- prepare_input(raw_data, col_select = c("CONTEXTE", "MATRICE1", "REGION", "SECTEUR", "LIEUPVT"),
                               id = "IDENTIFIANT", date = "DATE_PRELEVEMENT")
upset_data <- prepare_upset(prepared_data)
upset_profiles <- define_profiles(upset_data)
# number of distinct profiles
max(upset_profiles$group)
```

```{r tests-define_profiles}
test_that("define_profiles gives the same group to identical profiles", {
  upset <- data.frame(
    A = c(1, 1, 0, 1),
    B = c(0, 0, 1, 0),
    C = c(1, 1, 1, 0),
    row.names = c("s1", "s2", "s3", "s4")
  )
  profiles <- define_profiles(upset)
  expect_equal(colnames(profiles), c("profiles", "group", "names"))
  expect_equal(profiles$profiles, c("101", "101", "011", "100"))
  expect_equal(profiles$names, c("s1", "s2", "s3", "s4"))
  expect_equal(profiles$group[1], profiles$group[2])
  expect_equal(length(unique(profiles$group)), 3)
  expect_equal(define_profiles(upset, sep = "-")$profiles[1], "1-0-1")
})
```

## Selecting the strains: select_profiles

Finally, `select_profiles()` selects one strain per group. A group containing
a single strain gets this strain; since all strains of a larger group are
identical, one of them is chosen at random. Use `seed` to make the selection
reproducible.

```{r function-select_profiles}
#' Select one strain per group of identical profiles
#'
#' Selects at random one strain in each group defined by [define_profiles()].
#'
#' @param profiles A data frame returned by [define_profiles()].
#' @param prepared_data A data frame with one row per strain, as returned by
#'   [prepare_input()], with rows in the same order as `profiles`.
#' @param seed An integer passed to [set.seed()] to make the random choice of
#'   the representative strains reproducible, or `NULL` (default) to leave the
#'   random number generator untouched.
#'
#' @return `prepared_data` with three additional columns:
#'   \describe{
#'     \item{group}{the group of identical profiles of the strain;}
#'     \item{size}{the number of strains in this group;}
#'     \item{selected}{the identifier of the strain selected for this group.}
#'   }
#'   The selected strains are given by `unique(result$selected)`.
#' @export
#' @family profile method
#'
#' @examples
select_profiles <- function(profiles, prepared_data, seed = NULL){
  if (!is.null(seed)) {
    set.seed(seed)
  }
  selected_data <- prepared_data
  selected_data$group <- profiles$group
  selected_data$size <- as.vector(table(profiles$group)[as.character(profiles$group)])
  selection <- vapply(split(profiles$names, profiles$group),
                      function(x) x[sample.int(length(x), 1)], character(1))
  selected_data$selected <- unname(selection[as.character(profiles$group)])
  selected_data
}
```

```{r examples-select_profiles}
raw_data <- salmonella_strains
prepared_data <- prepare_input(raw_data, col_select = c("CONTEXTE", "MATRICE1", "REGION", "SECTEUR", "LIEUPVT"),
                               id = "IDENTIFIANT", date = "DATE_PRELEVEMENT")
upset_profiles <- define_profiles(prepare_upset(prepared_data))
selection <- select_profiles(upset_profiles, prepared_data, seed = 1)
# one strain per distinct profile
length(unique(selection$selected))
```

```{r tests-select_profiles}
test_that("define_profiles and select_profiles select one strain per profile", {
  raw_data <- salmonella_strains
  prepared_data <- suppressMessages(
    prepare_input(raw_data, col_select = c("CONTEXTE", "MATRICE1", "REGION", "SECTEUR", "LIEUPVT"),
                  id = "IDENTIFIANT", date = "DATE_PRELEVEMENT")
  )
  profiles <- define_profiles(prepare_upset(prepared_data))
  n_groups <- length(unique(profiles$profiles))
  expect_equal(max(profiles$group), n_groups)
  selected <- select_profiles(profiles, prepared_data)
  expect_equal(length(unique(selected$selected)), n_groups)
  expect_equal(sum(selected$size[!duplicated(selected$group)]), nrow(prepared_data))
  # each selected strain has the profile of the group it represents
  expect_equal(profiles[selected$selected, "group"], selected$group)
  expect_identical(select_profiles(profiles, prepared_data, seed = 1),
                   select_profiles(profiles, prepared_data, seed = 1))
})
```
